fedwire_intraday_profile.source: Armantier, Arnold & McAndrews (2008), FRBNY Economic Policy Review 14(2), 83-112, Table 1 'Percentiles of Value Time Distribution', 2006 mean column. https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/epr/08v14n2/0809arma.pdf
fedwire_intraday_profile.justification: Decile settlement times inverted by monotone (PCHIP) interpolation of the cumulative value distribution, evaluated at hour boundaries, renormalised over 09:00-18:30. Validation: derived post-17:00 share is 31.4%; the same paper independently reports >30% for 2005. That figure was not used in the inversion.

payments_per_day.source: Armantier et al. (2008), Table 2: mean daily Fedwire payment count 465,237 across all participants.
payments_per_day.justification: Order-of-magnitude anchor for one large participant's daily outgoing volume. Set to 400 releasable payments per simulated day. Result is scale-invariant in M up to a constant factor on information; only the shape of I(a) is claimed.

theta0_percentile.justification: Simulator is anchored at a stressed-but-not-extreme day: the 90th percentile of observed SOFR99-IORB. Swept in the robustness section.

theta0.source: Anchored to the 90th percentile of observed SOFR99-IORB (10.0 bps) over 2021-08-02 to 2026-08-04.
theta0.justification: theta is a latent normalised congestion index on [0,1], not an observable. The map from basis-point spreads to theta is assumed monotone; only the anchor point is empirical. theta0=0.90 places the system in a congested regime where response delays are dispersed enough to carry information.

r0_base_response_rate.justification: Response delays are Exp(r0*(1-theta)). r0 sets the time unit; setting it to 1 makes delays dimensionless. No empirical content.

kappa_coupling.source: FREE PARAMETER - no empirical counterpart exists.
kappa_coupling.justification: Strength of the relief effect: releasing at intensity a moves tightness by -kappa*a. No public data measures how much one participant's releases loosen system-wide congestion. This is the paper's principal free parameter and is swept across [0.3, 1.0] in the sensitivity analysis. The claim is that a regime exists, not that kappa takes any particular value.

theta0_bps_anchor.justification: 90th percentile of the observed tightness spread.

kappa_sensitivity.justification: Peak location tracks (1-theta0)/kappa across the swept range, confirming the inverted U is a structural property of the mechanism rather than an artefact of one parameter choice. Larger kappa moves the peak earlier and deepens the decline, as the analytic result predicts.

estimator.justification: Parametric rather than neural, so the information curve measures the mechanism and not training dynamics. Neural filter deferred to the full-environment stage.
